articles.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders.

Nov. 11

Hoop Collective: First Celtics-76ers game and NBA teams in the danger zone

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Bobby Marks to react to the first matchup between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers since the blockbuster trade this summer that sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia. They then move into the teams facing the most pressure currently and break them down into "danger tiers," including what concerns the Cleveland Cavaliers have and the slow start for the Miami Heat. In the final segment, they discuss if a Kristaps Porzingis trade could help the streaking Golden State Warriors this season.

You've got no tradable firsts, you've got one second to move in a deal. You're strapped against the hard cap. You're not going to be able to sign a 15th player.

"I already had concerns about their depth in their frontcourt here. It will be fascinating to watch as we get closer to February if this is stagnated here. Who's the odd man out, right? Like, is it Jarrett Allen? Is it Sam Merrill? I mean, Jaylon Tyson's on a rookie contract here. Like, the only big trade chip left for them is Jarrett Allen."

articles.headline: Sources: Giants called Falcons to ask about Bijan Robinson before trade deadline
articles.description: The Giants made a call to the Falcons before the NFL trade deadline inquiring about star running back Bijan Robinson, multiple sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：ジャイアンツがトレード期限前にビジャン・ロビンソンについてファルコンズに問い合わせ
articles.descriptionJa: 複数の関係者がESPNに語ったところによると、ジャイアンツはNFLのトレード期限前に、スターランニングバックのビジャン・ロビンソンについて問い合わせるため、ファルコンズに電話をした。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Giants made a call to the Atlanta Falcons before the NFL trade deadline inquiring about star running back Bijan Robinson, multiple sources told ESPN.

It was the latest call about potentially acquiring a running back made by the Giants, who have been linked to multiple high-level players at the position since hiring John Harbaugh earlier this year.

The Giants inquired about Kenneth Walker III in free agency, were interested in Jeremiyah Love at the top of this year's draft, made a trade offer to the Indianapolis Colts for Jonathan Taylor that ultimately was taken off the table, called the Tennessee Titans about Tony Pollard and looked into Justice Hill with the Baltimore Ravens before the deadline, according to sources.

It was unknown if New York actually made an offer to Atlanta for Robinson, the NFL's leading rusher.

Harbaugh was asked an hour before Tuesday's trade deadline about his desire to add a playmaker.

"I'd be excited ... for the right guy," he said. "My excitement level would be based on who the player is. You get the right player, then you're really excited. I wouldn't be excited for the not-right player. There's players you love and players you like. I would want a player that we love."

Robinson would seem to fit into that category, as a strong argument can be made that he's the best running back in the NFL. The 24-year-old has 1,130 yards from scrimmage this season, second in the NFL behind only Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs.

Multiple league sources believe, however, that Robinson is untouchable as the face of the Falcons.

Harbaugh has been adamant about building a big and physical team in New York and wants his offense to be centered around a power running game. But the Giants are 17th in rushing, averaging 112.1 yards per game and a pedestrian 3.9 yards per carry.

Cam Skattebo has primarily served as the lead back with Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary also playing significant roles. Tracy is currently on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.

The Giants (5-2-1) are first in the NFC East but didn't make a move at the trade deadline. They offered a second-round draft pick, a future fifth-rounder and an unknown player to the Colts for Taylor in recent weeks. The Colts wanted significantly more and ultimately didn't seem motivated to move him, several executives told ESPN.

New York eventually took the offer off the table, according to Harbaugh, and the teams never serious reengaged before the deadline.

The Giants now move forward with Skattebo as the lead back. The physical runner is set to return Thursday night against the Washington Commanders after missing a game with a hamstring injury.

Skattebo leads the Giants with 418 yards on the ground and is averaging 4.3 yards per carry but had the first two carries of his career over 20 yards in a Week 8 overtime win over the Houston Texans. The second-year player was also demoted for a game earlier this season because of fumbles.

articles.headline: The group chat that bonds Black NBA coaches off the court
articles.description: On the court, they're rivals. Off the court, they've found support among the only men who truly understand what they're going through: each other.
articles.headlineJa: コート外で黒人NBAコーチたちを結びつけるグループチャット
articles.descriptionJa: コート上ではライバルだが、コート外では、自分たちが直面している状況を真に理解してくれる唯一の存在である互いに支え合っている。
articles.body:
DETROIT PISTONS COACH J.B. Bickerstaff and then-Orlando Magic coach Jamahl Mosley broke the ice after nearly two weeks of silence: a simple bro hug at midcourt before their teams played Game 7 of last season first-round series.

More than a series was on the line -- jobs have been decided in these situations, and that series was no different. Regardless, the two consider themselves brothers.

"We didn't make eye contact during the series," Bickerstaff said. "I knew the outcome of that series -- we played two years before when I was in Cleveland -- if I would've lost to Jamahl, I would've been fired. I knew if Jamahl didn't beat us [last season], he was going to be fired.

"Coaching those games was extremely emotional, and them both coming down to Game 7s adds more weight to those moments. I know the impact that it has on you, your wife in that moment. His kids call me Uncle."

Several coaches closely watched the matchup. They are part of an 11-member group chat featuring Black NBA head coaches and assistants who have been friends for years.

"For us, it was fun," Indiana Pacers associate head coach Lloyd Pierce said. "It was Game 7. You don't have to put that face on anymore for your players. They knew. This is results oriented. Someone's going home, someone ain't. But it's all love. They had to be professionals, but it was a beautiful moment for our group."

Pierce and Washington Wizards assistant David Vanterpool couldn't wait to show the video of the two close friends' hug before the game at their annual "wine and conversation" event that takes place during summer league. It exemplified the community they have striven to create: two fierce competitors in their natural element who, behind the scenes, are friends in any other group chat, commiserating over shared experiences and struggles, talking about issues of the world in a space where they knew it would stay without judgment.

And doing so with the only men who can identify with what they are going through: each other.

There are nine Black head coaches in the NBA -- three fewer than last season with Jason Kidd, Chauncey Billups and Doc Rivers no longer with their franchises. When Kidd and Boston's Joe Mazzulla met in the 2024 NBA Finals, it was the first time two Black coaches faced each other in the Finals since 1975, when Al Attles' Golden State Warriors swept K.C. Jones' Washington Bullets. It's been cyclical, but the NBA had recently reached a high mark for Black coaches. There were 15 in 2022-23 and 14 the following season. In the 2019-20 season, that number was just seven.

This collective, which as a group chat has expanded into other events, has become an outlet to discuss opportunities that have come and ones that haven't. But it has also expanded into a network of support and connections that extends far beyond the court. articles.headline: Kings rookie star Darius Acuff Jr. frustrated over 1-10 start: 'I'm not a loser'
articles.description: Darius Acuff Jr. admitted that the Kings' poor start to the season is weighing down on him, saying he is "not a loser."
articles.headlineJa: キングスの新人スター、ダリアス・アカーフ・Jr.が1勝10敗のスタートに苛立ち、「私は敗者ではない」
articles.descriptionJa: ダリアス・アカーフ・Jr.は、キングスのシーズン序盤の不調が精神的な負担になっていることを認め、「自分は敗者ではない」と語った。
articles.body:
Darius Acuff Jr. admitted that the Sacramento Kings' poor start to the season is weighing on him.

After the Kings fell to 1-10 with Tuesday's loss to the Orlando Magic, Acuff was asked whether the losses were starting to take a toll.

"A lot," the rookie guard responded. "I'm not a loser, so it's not fun. But like I said, it's an 82-game season, so hopefully something will stick."

Acuff, 19, scored 29 points on 10-of-21 shooting and added six assists in Tuesday's 107-100 loss.

The No. 7 overall pick in this year's draft, Acuff is averaging 26.2 points -- the ninth most in the NBA -- and 7.3 assists per game this season.

But those impressive numbers have not translated into wins for the last-place Kings, who enter Wednesday tied with the Utah Jazz and Chicago Bulls for the worst record in the NBA.

"I don't know what to do," Acuff said. "I feel like we're trying -- everybody as a whole. We're just not coming out with the win. 1-10 just don't sound right."

Acuff's 288 points are the most by any rookie through the first 11 games of a season since Michael Jordan scored 289 for the Chicago Bulls in 1984. Kings veteran Zach LaVine praised Acuff after Tuesday's game, saying that the former Arkansas star is "going to be real special."

But Acuff, who committed four of Sacramento's 20 turnovers in Tuesday's loss, also noted that he and his teammates need to "clean up" their mistakes.

"We try," he said. "I think we've just got to come together at the end in the fourth quarter and just kind of get better as a team and close the games. We've got to figure it out at some point."

articles.headline: Man United near Mauricio Pochettino deal, Michael Carrick awaits verdict - sources
articles.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is set to take training again on Wednesday as he waits for news on his future, with the club in contact with Mauricio Pochettino, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
Manchester United are nearing an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino while Michael Carrick waits for news on his future, sources have told ESPN.

Pochettino is the leading candidate to replace Carrick and the club have opened talks with the 54-year-old's representatives, sources also told ESPN.

The former Argentina defender signed a new contract with the United States in August, but is known to be keen on taking over at Old Trafford. United are set to approach U.S. Soccer once they have a deal in place with Pochettino, sources told ESPN.

Club executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are meeting minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

The summit is pre-planned, but Carrick's position will dominate the agenda.

Sources have told ESPN that Carrick, who is leading training on Wednesday, is expected to be relieved of his duties following a poor start to the season which has seen United slip into the bottom three of the Premier League.

Club sources insist a final decision has not yet been taken and would first require sign off from both Ratcliffe and majority owners, the Glazer family.

United players not on international duty reported to Carrington on Tuesday for an afternoon training session led by Carrick and his staff.

- USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options

- Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye move for Forest's Murillo

- Man United shouldn't keep Carrick despite Villa comeback

Further sessions are scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday before the players are given time off ahead of their next game against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

U.S. Soccer confirmed planned media access with players scheduled for Wednesday had been cancelled in observance of Veterans Day, which removed the possibility of Pochettino's squad being asked to comment on the news of his potential exit.

Former Bournemouth and Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have also been considered to replace Carrick.

Keiran McKenna, the former Ipswich Town manager and Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler are also admired by the hierarchy, but sources have told ESPN that club bosses that United's current situation requires a manager with more experience.

Pochettino has extensive Premier League experience after spells at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has been considered for the United job before in 2018, 2022 and 2024.

The Lakers are fueled by Luka Doncic's historic start, which has featured 39.3 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per game.

In the East, the new look Philadelphia 76ers seem like they've been playing together for years, as LeBron James and Jaylen Brown have hit the ground running with their new teammates. They're tailed tightly by their offseason trade partners, the Boston Celtics, who seemingly haven't missed a beat with new faces around Jayson Tatum.

articles.headline: How Harry Kane rose to win Ballon d'Or and became an England legend
articles.description: Harry Kane went from overlooked youngster to Ballon d'Or winner. Now he's about to become England's record appearance-holder -- and possibly their greatest-ever player.
articles.body:
Another week, another landmark moment for Harry Kane. Life is like that right now for the England captain, who will become his country's all-time record appearance-maker when leading out the Three Lions against Croatia on Thursday.

It completes a remarkable fortnight for Kane, 33, after he won the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time and signed a new contract with Bayern Munich through to 2029. He is now one of the highest-paid players in Europe, at more than €30 million per year.

Surpassing Peter Shilton's 125-cap England record felt almost impossible for more than three decades, especially for an outfield player. Wayne Rooney reached 120, David Beckham 115, Steven Gerrard 114 and Ashley Cole 107, but Kane will go clear on his own with years still ahead of him.

- Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with crowning moment

- USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options

- Why Messi won't be 'do a Wrexham' as owner of non-league Cornellà

England's goal-scoring record appeared a similarly difficult climb. Sir Bobby Charlton's tally of 49 stood for 45 years before Rooney reached the half-century in 2015 and later ended on 53. Kane is on a remarkable 91 -- and counting.

He has captained England more often than any other player in history, leading England to back-to-back European Championship finals and a third-place finish at this summer's World Cup, the men's national team's best placing since their sole 1966 triumph.

The only thing missing is a major international trophy, something he willingly admits he would trade every individual accolade to have. But Kane's case for becoming England's greatest-ever player grows with each passing season.

After ending his 19-year association with Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur, Kane joined Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich for €120 million in August 2023. In March of that year, Bayern appointed Thomas Tuchel as manager. Former sporting director Hasan Salihamidžić has publicly claimed the club decided on Kane as their top summer target around a month later having first considered him in late 2021.

"He took convincing, but don't forget Bayern Munich is a huge club with a big reputation," Tuchel, now Kane's manager with England, told ESPN. "The prospect of winning titles, the prospect of competing in the Champions League every year, quarterfinals, semifinals, finals in basically all competitions gave us a good hand.

"But still, it is a big step for the English captain to step out of the Premier League and then the language is not easy. So it was a big step out of his comfort zone for Harry.

"In the end, with hindsight, because we are all smarter, it seems to have brought out the very, very best in him. He adapted so quickly, he became such an influential figure in such a big club. Full credit to him and his family. He took convincing, but we felt from the start it was possible."

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United add Brentford defender Nathan Collins to shortlist
articles.description: Brentford center back Nathan Collins has been added to Manchester United's list of defensive options. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Manchester United's list of defensive options now includes Brentford center back Nathan Collins, while Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Brentford center back Nathan Collins has been added to Manchester United's list of defensive options for the January transfer window, as reported by The Daily Mail. The Republic of Ireland captain has a contract until 2029, but 8th-placed Brentford would expect a hefty sum to let him go. Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich Town have conceded more Premier League goals this season than the 19 Man United have let in, and Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is also reported to be on the club's shortlist.

- Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, as reported by Bild's Christian Falk. Bayern were willing to pay €70 million to land the 18-year-old during the summer as they looked for a left winger who could complement Luis Díaz, before they went on to sign Ismael Saibari. But Bayern still need a left winger and could still look to land the England international in either January or the summer transfer window.

- Arsenal are eyeing a January move for Real Madrid forward Endrick, according to TalkSPORT. The versatile 20-year-old has played just 114 minutes this season and the Gunners are looking for attacking reinforcements on the wing following Bukayo Saka's injury. The Brazil international is one of a number of options being offered to Premier League clubs, but Diario AS has suggested there will be competition from AS Roma and Sporting CP, who both want to take Endrick on loan.

- In addition to referencing Endrick, The Independent has suggested Arsenal are also looking at Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and AFC Bournemouth's Junior Kroupi as they aim to sign a winger. With Real Madrid, Atlético and Chelsea all interested in central midfielder Martín Zubimendi, the Gunners would use the funds from any departure to sign a wide man.

- AC Milan are already making a move for Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi in January and want to pair him with Gonçalo Ramos, as reported by Gazzetta dello Sport. The negotiations are likely to be costly, though, as Brugge rejected a €35 million bid from Roma in the summer and Tresoldi has since gone on to score 13 goals in 15 games across the Jupiler Pro League and Champions League. It is expected that a fee of €50 million would now be required to sign the 22-year-old.

- Liverpool could consider letting Jeremie Frimpong leave amid interest from Al Hilal. (Football Insider)

- Crystal Palace have no intention of letting USMNT defender Chris Richards leave, despite interest from Internazionale. (Football Insider)

articles.headline: Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi denies wanting to leave amid Atlético Madrid links
articles.description: Martín Zubimendi has denied he is considering leaving Arsenal in the January transfer window amid reported interest from Atlético Madrid.
articles.body:
Martín Zubimendi has denied he is considering leaving Arsenal in the January transfer window amid reported interest from Atlético Madrid.

The Spanish midfielder has logged only 100 minutes in seven league appearances for Arsenal this term, a far cry from last season, where he played in all 38 Premier League games to help the Gunners win the title, averaging 79 minutes per game.

"I realise the winter transfer window is coming up, and rumours may start to circulate," he told Marca while on international duty with Spain.

"I've also read that a move [to Atlético] might be on the cards, but that's far from the case. I haven't wasted any energy on it, nor have I got in touch with anyone. I haven't wasted any energy on external matters. I've got enough on my plate just trying to earn a place in the team, get some playing time and fight to win this Premier League title, which is looking so promising."

Arsenal are top of the Premier League, five points clear of nearest rivals Brighton.

Asked if he will continue at Arsenal until the end of the season, Zubimendi, whose contract runs until June 2030, said: "Yes, I hope so. I'm happy there. I'm happy in London."

A 2026 World Cup winner with Spain, Zubimendi believes the workload of last season that led to physical fatigue, has affected his performances.

"I played an enormous number of minutes [last season], and, to be honest, I was tired," he said. "There were other factors, too, but the physical aspect could very well have been one of them."

Asked if he has considered seeking psychological help to deal with this bad patch, Zubimendi said: "I've thought about it and wouldn't rule it out, but for now, I haven't gone down that path.

"I'm well, I'm calm and happy with how I'm handling this situation. It's something I'd never experienced before, and I think you learn from situations like this too. What's more, it's at times like this that you need the people around you the most, and they're there for you."

- Konsa ruled out of England's clash with Croatia, Hill called up

- White: England fans don't know full story of 2022 World Cup squad exit

Zubimendi, 27, is focusing on the positives.

"When you've been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to playing less, I'm managing to see the bright side," he said. "I think everything comes and goes; just as the opposite happened to me last year and I played practically every minute, things can change very quickly."

Zubimendi admits he was warned by Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta that the he would face competition for playing time with the arrival of midfielder Bruno Guimarães.

"I spoke to Mikel [Arteta] at the start of the season," Zubimendi said.

articles.headline: Dirk Kuyt leaves Fenerbahce a week after defeating Liverpool
articles.description: Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.
articles.body:
ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.

articles.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder (8-3, fifth in the Western Conference) vs. Portland Trail Blazers (7-3, eighth in the Western Conference)


              Portland, Oregon; Wednesday, 10 p.m. EST


              LINE: Thunder -1.5; over/under is 226.5


              BOTTOM LINE: Oklahoma City visits Portland for a Western Conference matchup.


              Portland finished 42-40 overall and 29-23 in Western Conference action last season. The Trail Blazers averaged 19.2 points off of turnovers, 18.5 second-chance points and 34.9 bench points last season.


              Oklahoma City finished 64-18 overall, 12-4 in Northwest Division games and 30-10 on the road a season ago. The Thunder averaged 119.0 points per game while allowing opponents to score 107.9 last season.


              The teams square off for the second time this season. The Trail Blazers won the last meeting 123-103 on Nov. 11. Damian Lillard scored 25 points to help lead the Trail Blazers to the win.


              INJURIES: Trail Blazers: Shaedon Sharpe: out (meniscus), Vit Krejci: out (leg), Ja Morant: out (hamstring).


              Thunder: Cason Wallace: out (shoulder), Nikola Topic: out (back), Thomas Sorber: out (knee), Chet Holmgren: out (knee), Jaylin Williams: out (back), Jalen Williams: out (ankle).
